8.meaning: A book, scripture, or written record — that which is written. It denotes a written document, and in the religious sense a revealed Scripture sent down from Allah.
8.grammar: A noun ('a book') with the -un ending, the nominative indefinite case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence. The form names a written or revealed text without specifying which.

9.meaning: Confirming, attesting as true — an active participle describing one (or something) that verifies and confirms the truth of what came before. It conveys bearing witness that another thing is true and corroborating it.
9.grammar: An active participle (form II) meaning 'one who confirms/verifies'. The mu- prefix marks the doer of the action. The final -un (tanwīn) is the indefinite nominative ending, marking the word as indefinite and in the nominative case — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it.
9.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — to be truthful; (form II) to confirm, hold true

11.meaning: An adjective meaning 'Arabic' — pertaining to the Arabs or to their language; that which is in clear, eloquent Arabic speech.
11.grammar: A relational adjective formed with the -iyy suffix ('belonging to / characterized by'). The final -an (tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative: it marks an indefinite descriptive word agreeing with an indefinite accusative noun it qualifies ('an Arabic …').

12.meaning: So that he/it may warn — to give warning, to caution someone about danger or coming consequence so they may take heed. The opening particle expresses purpose ('in order to'), and the verb is the masculine-singular 'he warns'.
12.grammar: A purpose particle 'li-' attached to a present-tense verb in the form-IV pattern (yufʿil), which makes the action causative: to make someone aware of danger. The ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('he'); the final -a is the subjunctive vowel that the verb takes after a purpose particle like 'li-', giving the sense 'so that he may warn'.
12.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — to warn, caution, give notice of consequence

13.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
13.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

14.meaning: They did wrong / acted unjustly / committed oppression — Ẓulm is placing a thing where it does not belong: wronging others, oneself, or the truth, including the gravest wrong of associating others with Allah.
14.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine plural: 'they wronged.' The -ū ending marks a completed action by a group of males (or a mixed group). (The silent alif written after the -ū is an orthographic convention and is not pronounced.)

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

4.meaning: 'Our Lord' — 'Rabb' (Lord, Master, Sustainer who creates, owns, nurtures and governs) joined to 'our'. A weighty term for Allah as the One who brings up and sustains all that exists.
4.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun '-nā' ('our'). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, used when the word is the subject or predicate of a sentence ('[He] is our Lord').
4.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
5.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

6.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
6.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

7.meaning: 'They stood firm / were upright / kept straight' — a past-tense verb meaning to be or become straight and upright, to hold a steady, correct course, or to remain firmly committed, referring to a group of males (or a mixed group). The Form X pattern here carries the sense of standing oneself upright and steadfast.
7.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the Form X (is-ta-…) pattern, here meaning to make oneself upright / hold a straight course. The ending -ū means 'they', a group of males or a mixed group (third-person masculine plural). The final silent alif (-ū + ا) is just a spelling convention after this plural ending.
7.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, be upright

8.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
8.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

9.meaning: 'Fear' — a state of being afraid, dread, or alarm; apprehension of something harmful or threatening.
9.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The '-un' ending (nunation) marks it as nominative and indefinite — 'a fear' or simply 'fear' — and the nominative typically signals the doer or subject of a sentence, or the subject of an existential statement ('there is fear').

10.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
10.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
10.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

11.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
11.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

12.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
12.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

13.meaning: 'They grieve / will grieve' — to feel sorrow, sadness, or distress; to be saddened over loss or hardship.
13.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine plural. The 'ya-' prefix marks third person, and the '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they') with the verb in its full (indicative) form, describing ongoing or future action. Read together the word is 'yaḥzanūna.'

1.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
1.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

2.meaning: 'Companions / people of, dwellers, owners' — those closely associated with something, its inseparable folk, fellows, or inmates; literally the people who 'keep company with' a thing.
2.grammar: A masculine plural noun (the plural of ṣāḥib, 'companion'). The '-u' ending is nominative, typically marking the subject of a sentence; it appears here without nunation because the word is in a possessive construction ('companions OF …') with a following noun.

3.meaning: The Garden / Paradise — a definite noun literally meaning 'the garden'; the term for the Garden of Paradise, the abode of reward in the Hereafter.
3.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the'. The '-i' ending (on the feminine '-at-') is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition. 'janna' originally means a lush, shaded garden.
3.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal (a garden's dense foliage 'covers' the ground)

4.meaning: Ones who abide / remain forever — those who dwell perpetually and permanently in a state or place, without end. The word denotes lasting, undying permanence.
4.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word: 'ones abiding'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive form, used when the word is an object or governed by a preceding element. It describes people characterized by perpetual abiding.
4.root: خ-ل-د (kh-l-d) — perpetuity, everlasting abiding

5.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
5.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

6.meaning: "as a recompense / requital / repayment" — a noun denoting the return or payment given for a deed, whether reward or penalty.
6.grammar: A masculine noun. The final "-an" (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative ending; on a word like this it commonly functions adverbially, expressing the cause, purpose, or manner — i.e., "(done) as a recompense."
6.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — to recompense, requite, repay, reward or punish

7.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
7.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

8.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
8.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
8.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

9.meaning: 'They do / they work, they act' — a present-tense verb of doing and working, covering deeds and actions carried out by a group.
9.grammar: Present/imperfect verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (do).' The -ūna ending also marks the indicative mood, the plain statement form, as opposed to command or negated-future forms.
9.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

2.meaning: the human being, mankind — the human creature in general, marked by sociability and forgetfulness.
2.grammar: A noun for the human being, with the definite article al- ('the'). The -a ending is accusative, typically marking the direct object of a verb or following certain particles. Used generically, it denotes humankind as a type.
2.root: أ-ن-س ('-n-s) — to be sociable, familiar; humanness

3.meaning: A combination meaning roughly 'with/toward his two parents (father and mother together)'. The dual noun wālidān refers specifically to the two who gave one birth — one's father and mother as a pair — and the attached pronoun makes them 'his'.
3.grammar: The prefix bi- is a preposition ('with, to, toward'). The stem is a dual noun (referring to exactly two — a father and mother together); its dual ending appears as -ay rather than -ān because it stands in the genitive/accusative form, which is also what the preposition bi- requires. The final -hi is the attached possessive pronoun 'his' (the -i vowel is the form this pronoun takes after an -i sound).
3.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth, beget; offspring

4.meaning: Good treatment, excellence, doing what is beautiful and right — acting toward others with kindness, generosity, and the highest moral excellence (iḥsān), going beyond mere duty to genuine goodness.
4.grammar: A verbal noun (the act of doing good). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥ) marks the indefinite accusative; it often functions adverbially or as an object, conveying 'doing good' or '[show] good treatment' — describing the manner or content of an action.
4.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good, beautiful, excellent

13.meaning: "a month" — a single lunar month, in the indefinite singular. The accusative form here is the one used to specify the unit being counted after a number ('… months').
13.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The -an (tanwīn fatḥ) ending marks the accusative case and the lack of 'the'; after numbers it functions as the counted noun ('… as months'), and more generally the accusative can mark an object or a specifying complement.
13.root: ش-ه-ر (sh-h-r) — month, lunar/visible cycle; to make well-known

14.meaning: A particle meaning 'until, up to the point that,' or 'so that.' It marks an end-limit in time, place, or purpose — the boundary at which something culminates or the goal toward which it moves.
14.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It introduces an end-point or goal; when followed by a verb it can express purpose or result ('until' / 'so that').

15.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
15.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

16.meaning: A verb meaning 'it reached / attained / arrived at' — to extend to and make contact with a point, person, or limit, whether a message reaching hearers or a thing arriving at its end. It conveys completion of arrival.
16.grammar: Past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it reached'). The plain stem with the final -a marks completed past action and a masculine singular doer.
16.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — to reach, attain, convey to its destination

17.meaning: 'His full strength / prime of maturity' — the age at which a person reaches sound, settled adulthood and full vigor of body and judgment; with the attached pronoun 'his'.
17.grammar: A noun carrying the attached possessive pronoun -hu 'his'. The noun is accusative in function (e.g. as the goal of 'until he reaches …'), but that case is not separately visible here: because the stem ends in a doubled consonant (-dd), a short -a is inserted as a connecting/linking vowel before the suffix, so the -a you hear is a phonological helper, not the case marker.

19.grammar: A cardinal number of the 'tens' family. The '-īna' ending is the form these tens (20, 30, 40 …) take when they are an object or follow a preposition (the accusative/genitive form); the counted thing after it is usually a singular indefinite noun.

20.meaning: 'A year' (and, in counting, 'years'). The noun sanah denotes a year, a full cycle of time.
20.grammar: An indefinite noun. The final -an is nunation in the accusative case: the form a noun takes as a direct object, and also the standard case for a noun specifying an amount or a span (e.g. after a number) — hence the plural sense 'years' when counted.

21.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
21.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

22.meaning: Rabb (Lord) joined to 'my': the One who owns, sustains, nurtures, and governs — combining mastery, ownership, and loving cultivation. With the attached 'my' it is an intimate address, 'my Lord.'
22.grammar: A noun, rabb, with the first-person possessive (the original 'my' yāʾ being reduced to a final -i, so 'my Lord'). The word denotes the Master who creates, owns, and lovingly sustains. Used as a heartfelt vocative, calling upon one's Lord.
22.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, be lord over

24.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
24.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

27.meaning: A feminine singular relative pronoun: 'the one which / that which / who' (referring to a single feminine thing). It introduces a descriptive clause that tells us more about a preceding feminine noun.
27.grammar: A relative pronoun, feminine singular, fixed in form (it does not change for case). It links a feminine noun to a following clause describing it, the equivalent of English 'which,' 'that,' or 'who.'

29.meaning: A preposition meaning 'upon / on / over' fused with the attached pronoun 'me,' giving 'upon me / against me / on my account.' The base preposition signals being on top of, responsible for, or burdened by something, and can also carry the sense of something owed by or weighing against a person.
29.grammar: A preposition with the first-person singular pronoun 'me' attached. When the pronoun 'me' joins this preposition, its form shifts so the two merge into 'ʿalayya.' Pronouns attached to prepositions always take the object form ('me,' not 'I'), and no case ending applies to them.

30.meaning: A compound, 'and upon / and on / and against' — the connector 'and' joined to the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, against'). It adds a further thing onto which something rests or against which it bears.
30.grammar: The prefix wa- is the connective 'and', joining what follows to what came before. ʿalā is an indeclinable preposition that puts the following noun in the genitive case and signals 'on, over, or upon' something.

32.meaning: A two-part connector: 'and that.' The 'wa' joins what precedes, and 'an' is the subordinating particle 'that,' which introduces a following verb-clause (often steering it into the subjunctive) — used to report or quote a command, statement, or purpose.
32.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus the particle an, a subordinator meaning 'that' which heads a clause and commonly puts a following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood (often expressing purpose, intention, or reported speech). It is a particle and does not itself take a case ending.

34.meaning: "Righteous / good / sound" — an active participle describing one who or that which is upright and wholesome and acts rightly; as a description of deeds it means good, virtuous works.
34.grammar: An active participle used as a noun or adjective. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a righteous one / a good deed') and in the accusative case — the form used for a direct object or other complement.
34.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound / upright / righteous

36.meaning: And set right / put in order / reform: a command to make matters good, repair what is broken, and act righteously. The verb (causative form) means to bring about soundness and well-being.
36.grammar: A prefixed 'and' (wa) joined to a command (imperative) in a causative form, addressed to a single male: 'set right!' The final consonant carries a silent ending (sukūn), the normal closing of an imperative.
36.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, set right

37.meaning: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
37.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

38.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
38.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

39.meaning: My offspring, descendants, or progeny. 'Dhurriyya' is one's children and their line of descent; the attached pronoun makes it 'my.'
39.grammar: A noun with the first-person singular possessive ending -ī ('my'). The original feminine ending of the noun appears as -t before this pronoun. The attached -ī ('my') is the same form whether the noun is subject, object, or possessor.
39.root: ذ-ر-ر / ذ-ر-ا (dh-r-r / dh-r-ʾ) — to scatter, multiply, produce offspring

40.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
40.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

41.meaning: 'I have repented / turned back' — from tāba; a first-person declaration of returning to Allah from sin.
41.grammar: A past-tense (completed) verb. The -tu ending marks the speaker as the subject — 'I (did it).' It states that the act of turning back in repentance has been carried out by the one speaking.
41.root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b) — to turn back, repent, return

42.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
42.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

43.meaning: And indeed I — a connector 'and' joined to an emphatic particle that strongly affirms what follows ('truly, indeed'), with 'I' attached as its subject.
43.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus the emphatic particle inna, which lends strong certainty to the statement it opens. The attached -ī ('me/I') is its grammatical subject; inna places the noun or pronoun after it in the accusative.

44.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
44.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

45.meaning: The ones who submit/surrender — those who give themselves wholly to Allah in willing obedience and peace (the Muslims). As an active participle it names people characterized by this submission.
45.grammar: The prefix al- is 'the'. The stem is the Form IV active participle 'one who submits/surrenders'. The ending -īna is the sound masculine plural in the genitive/accusative state (the form used after prepositions, as object, or when linked to a preceding noun); its nominative counterpart would be -ūna. So: 'the ones who submit'.

1.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
1.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
4.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.
4.root: — (a preposition; no triliteral verbal root)

5.meaning: A verb meaning 'he did good / acted well, excellently' — to do what is beautiful, fine, and right; also 'he was good (at something)'.
5.grammar: A Form IV (afʿala) past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular 'he'; the bare -a ending marks a completed action by 'he'. Form IV here gives the sense of doing/making good, acting with excellence.

6.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
6.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

7.meaning: They did / they worked — to perform a deed or action, to do work. The base word covers purposeful action and labor.
7.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb. The -ū ending marks 'they' (a group of males) as the doers (the silent alif after it is a spelling convention).
7.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, act, work, perform a deed

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

9.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

10.meaning: Their evil deeds, misdeeds, or wrongs — bad actions and the harm or offence they carry; with the attached pronoun, the misdeeds belonging to them.
10.grammar: A feminine sound plural noun (singular sayyiʾa) with the attached possessive 'their'. The -i vowel before -him reflects the genitive/possessive linkage to that pronoun.

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
11.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

12.meaning: Companions, associates, fellows; those who keep company with or belong to a thing — people closely bound to something (often 'people/inhabitants of …').
12.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of ṣāḥib ('companion'). The final -i is the genitive ending, which typically links the word to a following noun ('companions OF …') or follows a preposition. As a plural it denotes a group, here in a possessive/linking relationship.
12.root: ص-ح-ب (ṣ-ḥ-b) — companionship, to accompany, keep company

13.meaning: The Garden / Paradise — a definite noun literally meaning 'the garden'; the term for the Garden of Paradise, the abode of reward in the Hereafter.
13.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the'. The '-i' ending (on the feminine '-at-') is genitive, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition. 'janna' originally means a lush, shaded garden.
13.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal (a garden's dense foliage 'covers' the ground)

14.meaning: 'a promise / pledge' — a binding assurance of something to come; here as a noun naming the thing pledged or the act of pledging.
14.grammar: A verbal noun with the -a (accusative) ending, which typically marks it as a direct object or as an emphatic inner object reinforcing a verb of the same meaning ('a promise [truly promised]'). It names the act/content of promising.
14.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, pledge, give an assurance

16.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
16.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

17.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
17.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
17.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

18.meaning: 'They are promised / threatened' — something pledged to a group, whether a promised good or a warned-of consequence, with the group as recipient.
18.grammar: A present-tense passive verb (the subjects receive the action). The yu- prefix with the inner vowel pattern signals 'are being …' (done to them). The -ūna ending marks 'they' (plural) in ongoing/repeated time.
18.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, pledge, warn of what is to come

1.meaning: A connector meaning 'and the one who/which', joining a clause and pointing to a single masculine person or thing ('and that which…').
1.grammar: Built from the joining particle wa- ('and/but') plus the masculine singular relative pronoun alladhī ('the one who/which'). A relative pronoun introduces a description and stands for a definite masculine person or thing; its form is fixed and does not change for grammatical case.

2.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
2.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

4.meaning: An exclamation of irritation, weariness, or disgust — like saying 'ugh!' or 'phew!'. A sound expressing annoyance or contempt toward something or someone.
4.grammar: An interjection (a sound-word expressing emotion), not a regular noun or verb. The -in ending (with nunation) marks it as indefinite, giving the sense of 'an utterance of disgust'. As an exclamation its form is essentially fixed.
4.root: — (interjection; no triliteral root)

5.meaning: To the two of you / for the two of you — a preposition meaning 'to, for, belonging to' fused with the dual 'you two' pronoun, expressing direction or benefit toward two addressees.
5.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') joined to the second-person dual pronoun -kumā ('you two'). The -kumā suffix specifically addresses exactly two people; the whole expresses direction, benefit, or possession toward both. (The doubled l- reflects assimilation with a preceding word in connected recitation.)

7.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
7.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

9.meaning: 'And indeed / while already' — the word 'wa' ('and, while') joined to 'qad', a particle that, before a past-tense verb, stresses that the action has certainly and already happened.
9.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and', or circumstantial 'while') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' emphasizes completion and certainty ('has indeed already…'); with a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes' or 'may'.

12.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
12.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

13.meaning: Before me — the notion of 'before' in time or place (earlier than, in front of), here joined to a 'me' to mean prior to my own time.
13.grammar: An adverb of time/place ('before') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me/my'). 'qabl' takes the genitive case after it; the '-ī' suffix is the first-person singular possessive/object, giving 'before me'.
13.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; front

16.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
16.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

19.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
19.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

20.meaning: 'a promise / pledge' — a binding assurance of something to come; here as a noun naming the thing pledged or the act of pledging.
20.grammar: A verbal noun with the -a (accusative) ending, which typically marks it as a direct object or as an emphatic inner object reinforcing a verb of the same meaning ('a promise [truly promised]'). It names the act/content of promising.
20.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, pledge, give an assurance

21.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
21.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

22.meaning: 'Truth, reality, a rightful due' — that which is firmly real, correct, and established; also a right or claim that is owed. As a descriptor it means 'true, real, well-founded.'
22.grammar: An indefinite noun. The -un ending (nominative with tanwīn, the 'n' sound) is the form a noun takes as the subject or as the completing word of a statement ('is true/real').
22.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, what is due

23.meaning: Then/so He says — the verb 'say' joined to a connector meaning 'then' or 'so,' indicating a statement that follows as a consequence.
23.grammar: A present/future (imperfect) verb prefixed by 'then/so.' The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he.' The final -u ending is the indicative mood, signalling a plain statement of fact.

24.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
24.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

25.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
25.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

26.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
26.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

27.meaning: "Legends, fables, written-down tales of old." Stories or accounts that have been set down and passed along — often with the nuance of mere old fables rather than authentic record.
27.grammar: A plural noun. The final -u ending marks the nominative case — the case a noun takes as the subject of a sentence or as the thing being identified (as in "these are …"). Being the first term of a possessive phrase, it carries no indefinite tanwīn.
27.root: س-ط-ر (s-ṭ-r) — to write, draw lines, set down in rows

28.meaning: "The former ones, the people of old, the earlier generations." Those who came before, the ancients and predecessors.
28.grammar: A definite ("the") masculine plural noun/adjective. The "-īna" ending is the sound-masculine-plural form used in the accusative or genitive — i.e., when the word is an object, follows a preposition, or is linked to a preceding noun as its possessor ("… of the former ones").
28.root: ا-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — to be first, foremost; beginning

1.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
1.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: Due right, just measure, rightful claim; that which is true and rightly owed — here used to mean 'as is truly its due'.
3.grammar: A noun meaning 'truth, right, due'. The final -a (accusative) often marks the object of a verb, and in a possessive phrase like this it commonly conveys the sense 'with the full right/due OF …', i.e. as something deserves to be done.
3.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, that which is due and real

4.meaning: 'Upon them / against them' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, against') carrying an attached plural pronoun referring to a group of males.
4.grammar: ʿalā ('upon') takes the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The -him ending is the attached pronoun for a masculine plural 'them'; its final vowel appears as -u (himu) to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with the definite article.

5.meaning: The word, the saying, the utterance — a statement or pronouncement; qawl is speech that has been spoken, and 'the word' can mean a settled decree or verdict.
5.grammar: A definite noun ('the …'). The final -u is the nominative ending, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence.
5.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak; a saying, statement, or pronouncement.

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
6.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
6.root: — (particle)

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'nations, communities, or peoples' — the plural of 'umma,' a group bound together as one community.
7.grammar: A plural noun. The ending -in is genitive and indefinite (the doubled 'nunation' marking 'some, an indefinite'). The genitive case typically follows a preposition or links the noun to a preceding noun (the 'of' relationship), and the -in shows it is indefinite ('some communities').

8.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

9.meaning: 'It passed away / went by, came to an end' — said of a community, time, or era that has elapsed and is now gone. The root carries the sense of being emptied out, hence of time or people that have passed.
9.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -t (sukūn-marked -at) suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it,' used here because the noun it refers to is grammatically feminine. The past tense states a completed action.
9.root: خ-ل-و (kh-l-w) — to be empty/vacant; to pass away, elapse

10.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
10.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

11.meaning: 'Before them' in time — denoting what came earlier, the period or persons preceding a masculine plural group.
11.grammar: An adverb of time, 'before,' carrying the genitive ending -i because it is linked to a following possessor. The attached 'him' means 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group), giving 'before them.' The -i ending reflects that the word is governed in a possessive link.
11.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; before/prior

12.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
12.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

13.meaning: A noun meaning 'the jinn' — a class of unseen beings created from smokeless fire, possessing free will and accountability like humankind.
13.grammar: A definite noun with the article al- ('the'). The -i (genitive) ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in a possessive 'of' relationship.
13.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal, be hidden from sight

14.meaning: And humankind — human beings collectively, mankind, especially as contrasted with the unseen jinn. Carries a sense of sociability and familiarity.
14.grammar: A collective noun with the prefixed 'and' plus 'the'. The final -i is the genitive case ending, which typically follows a preposition or oath particle, or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.

15.meaning: 'Indeed they' — the emphatic particle 'inna' ('truly, indeed') joined to the pronoun 'them/they', strongly affirming a statement about a group.
15.grammar: The emphatic particle inna ('indeed / truly'), which strengthens and affirms a sentence, with the attached pronoun -hum ('they'). Inna places its attached noun or pronoun in the accusative, so -hum here functions as 'they' serving as the subject of the emphasized statement ('indeed they...').

16.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
16.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
16.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

17.meaning: Losers — those who suffer loss and ruin, ending up with a deficit. A 'khāsir' is one whose venture or final account comes out at a loss.
17.grammar: An active participle (one in the state of the action) in the masculine plural. The -īna ending marks the accusative/genitive plural — used for a direct object, after a preposition, or (as often here) describing a state, e.g. 'as losers'.

1.meaning: A combination meaning 'and for each / and to everyone' — joining 'and' with the preposition 'for/to' and the word 'all, each one', indicating that something belongs to or applies to every one.
1.grammar: A cluster: wa- 'and', the preposition li- 'for/to', and the noun kull 'all/each'. The ending -in is genitive (the case required after the preposition li-), and its final -n (tanwīn) marks the word as indefinite ('every one, each'). The doubled l (shadda) is part of kull.

2.meaning: Means 'ranks / degrees / levels' — gradations of standing or rank, one tier above another, like rungs by which things differ in elevation.
2.grammar: A feminine plural noun: 'degrees / ranks.' The -un ending is the nominative with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite): 'degrees / ranks (are…).' The nominative is the case for the subject of a sentence. The long -ā- is the plural-pattern vowel.
2.root: د-ر-ج (d-r-j) — to ascend by steps, gradation, rank

3.meaning: A fused word combining the preposition 'min' ('from', 'of', 'about') with the relative/indefinite 'mā' ('what', 'that which'). Together: 'from what', 'about that which', 'of what'.
3.grammar: The preposition 'min' and the word 'mā' merge in pronunciation (the 'n' assimilating into the 'm'). 'min' governs a genitive, and 'mā' here functions as a relative pronoun introducing a clause ('that which …'). These are indeclinable particles without case endings.

4.meaning: They did / they worked — to perform a deed or action, to do work. The base word covers purposeful action and labor.
4.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb. The -ū ending marks 'they' (a group of males) as the doers (the silent alif after it is a spelling convention).
4.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, act, work, perform a deed

6.meaning: 'Their deeds / works' — the plural noun 'deeds, actions, or works' with the attached pronoun 'their' (a masculine group).
6.grammar: A masculine plural noun ('deeds'; aʿmāl is the broken plural of ʿamal) carrying the possessive pronoun -hum ('their'). The -a before the pronoun is the accusative ending, generally marking the word as a direct object.
6.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, act, work; deed

7.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
7.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

8.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

9.meaning: They are wronged / treated unjustly — to suffer ẓulm, the placing of something out of its right place: injustice, oppression, being deprived of one's due. The passive form names being on the receiving end of wrongdoing.
9.grammar: Present-tense passive verb, third-person masculine plural. The yu- prefix (with the internal vowelling) marks the third person and the passive 'are being …', and the -ūna ending makes it 'they' (masculine plural) as the ones undergoing the action: 'they are wronged'. The -na is the indicative marker.

1.meaning: "and (on the) day" — the conjunction "and" joined to the noun for "day," a single daytime period or, more broadly, an appointed day or time of judgment/event.
1.grammar: The wa- prefix is the conjunction "and." The -a ending on the noun is accusative; on a word for "day" this frequently marks it as an adverb of time ("on the day …"), or marks it as the object of a verb.

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
4.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

5.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
5.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
5.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

6.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
6.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').
6.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — fire, blaze, burning

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
9.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

11.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
11.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
11.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

13.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
13.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

14.meaning: So / then — the day; a connective particle joined to the noun 'the day.' It links to what precedes (drawing a consequence or sequence, 'so / then') and names the day.
14.grammar: The prefix fa- is a connector meaning 'so / then,' marking a result or sequence. al- is 'the.' The final -a is the accusative case, which often marks a direct object or, with time-words like 'day,' an adverbial sense ('on the day').

15.meaning: 'You are recompensed / repaid' — a passive verb meaning a group is given back what their deeds deserve, whether reward or penalty. The doer (the One who repays) is understood, not named.
15.grammar: A present/imperfect passive verb (form I). The tu- prefix with passive vowelling plus the -una ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject being acted upon ('you [all] are repaid'). The -una (not -u) shows the indicative mood, used for plain factual statements.
15.root: ج-ز-ى (j-z-y) — recompense, requital, repaying in kind

16.meaning: Torment, punishment, or chastisement — severe, painful suffering imposed as a penalty.
16.grammar: A singular noun. The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case, the form used for a direct object of a verb, or for the first noun of a possessive pair ('the punishment of …') when that whole phrase is itself an object.

17.meaning: The disgrace / humiliation / abasement — a noun naming the state of being lowered and dishonoured, the opposite of honour and might. Carries the definite article 'the'.
17.grammar: A definite noun (with 'al-', 'the'). The final -i (kasra) is genitive: it marks the word as linked to a preceding preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to another noun.
17.root: ه-و-ن (h-w-n) — lowliness, disgrace, being held cheap

18.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
18.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

19.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
19.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
19.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

20.meaning: You act arrogantly / haughtily — to be proud, to puff oneself up, to scorn the truth and disdain to submit. The form X pattern conveys deeming oneself great and above others.
20.grammar: A present/imperfect verb (form X). The ta- prefix with the -una ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'). The -una ending (not -u) signals the indicative mood, used for ongoing or factual statements. Form X here carries the reflexive sense of 'consider oneself great'.
20.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — greatness, bigness; here pride and self-magnification

21.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
21.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

22.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
22.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

23.meaning: 'Without' or 'other than' — the preposition bi- joined to ghayr, a noun meaning 'other than / not / lacking', together conveying the absence of something ('with no …', 'wrongfully').
23.grammar: bi- is a preposition that takes the genitive; ghayr is a noun of exception/negation ('other than'). Its -i ending is genitive (required after bi-) and it also links to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship, so 'bi-ghayri X' means 'without X / other than X'.
23.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

24.meaning: 'The truth', 'the right', 'what is rightfully due' — that which is real, correct, and justly owed; the opposite of falsehood and wrongdoing.
24.grammar: A definite masculine noun (the al- prefix means 'the'). The -i ending is genitive, the case typically taken after a preposition or when the word links to a preceding noun ('… of the truth / by right').
24.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, rightness, that which is established and due

25.meaning: And by/with what…, and because of what… — a connective combining 'and', the preposition 'bi' ('with, by, because of'), and 'mā' ('what / that which'). Together they introduce the means or cause by which something is done.
25.grammar: A compound of particles: the conjunction wa ('and'), the preposition bi ('with, by, because of'), and the relative/indefinite mā ('what, that which'). It has no case ending of its own; the bi typically puts a following noun in the genitive, and here governs the unchanging word mā.

26.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
26.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
26.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

1.meaning: 'And mention / and remember / and recall' — a command to bring something to mind and call it out, whether by remembering it inwardly or speaking of it aloud.
1.grammar: The prefix wa- is 'and'. The stem is a command (imperative) addressed to a single male: 'mention / remember!'. The helping vowel at the start (the alif pronounced u-) is needed to begin the word, and the final consonant carries a vowelless ending (sukūn), which is the typical close of a singular command.
1.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind; remembrance

3.meaning: An active participle meaning 'one who transgresses, oversteps, goes beyond the limit'. It describes a person who exceeds proper bounds, acting in hostility or excess.
3.grammar: An active participle (doer pattern, originally ʿādiy → ʿādin), masculine singular, used as a noun/adjective. The -in ending is indefinite nunation in the genitive case — marking 'a transgressor' and the case used after prepositions or in noun-to-noun linkage.
3.root: ع-د-و (ʿ-d-w) — to overstep, transgress, show enmity

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
4.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

6.meaning: His people / his folk — the community, nation, or kinfolk belonging to him, with the attached pronoun marking possession.
6.grammar: A noun with the accusative -a ending, the form used when the word is a direct object, followed by the possessive suffix -hu ('his,' masculine singular).
6.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand/rise; a group that stands together, a people

8.meaning: 'And indeed / while already' — the word 'wa' ('and, while') joined to 'qad', a particle that, before a past-tense verb, stresses that the action has certainly and already happened.
8.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and', or circumstantial 'while') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' emphasizes completion and certainty ('has indeed already…'); with a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes' or 'may'.

11.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
11.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

12.meaning: A noun meaning 'between, in the midst of, the space separating two things.' It denotes the interval or position dividing one side from another, and is regularly used to express 'between X and Y.'
12.grammar: A noun of place that functions adverbially ('between / in the midst of'). The final -i ending is genitive, which typically links the word to a following noun ('… between … OF …') or marks it as governed by a preposition. Here the -i shows it is bound to whatever noun follows it.

13.meaning: 'His two hands' — literally a dual 'two hands' with 'his' attached. Often used idiomatically for what lies 'in front of' or 'before' someone (i.e. between his hands).
13.grammar: The noun 'yad' (hand) in its dual form 'two hands'. The -ay ending is the dual in the genitive/accusative state (as opposed to -ā for the subject case), used after prepositions or in possessive links. The attached 'hi' means 'his' (the -i vowel of 'hi' harmonizing after the -ay). In construct, the dual's final -n drops before the pronoun.

14.meaning: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
14.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

15.meaning: A noun meaning 'behind him / his rear, his back-part' — the region or direction that is at the back of someone, paired with his attached possessor.
15.grammar: A noun of place ('behind, rear') with the attached pronoun -hi ('his / him'). The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a following possessor or follows a preposition. The pronoun appears as -hi (rather than -hu) precisely because of this preceding -i vowel.
15.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — being behind, succeeding, coming after

16.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that … not,' 'lest,' 'so as not to.' It introduces a clause of something feared, intended-to-prevent, or negated after a verb.
16.grammar: A merging of the particle an ('that,' which introduces a verb in the subjunctive) with the negative lā ('not'); the 'n' of an assimilates into lā, giving allā. Together they mean 'that … not' and put the following verb into the subjunctive mood, often after verbs of fearing, wishing, or commanding.

17.meaning: (That) you should serve and worship — to direct devotion, obedience, and humble submission to one worthy of it; the act of ʻībāda (worship) addressed to a group.
17.grammar: A present/subjunctive verb. The ta- prefix marks a 'you' subject, and the -ū ending makes it plural ('you all'). When governed by a preceding particle the form takes the subjunctive ('that you may worship'); the dropped final nūn (written ū rather than ūna) reflects that subjunctive/jussive state.

18.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
18.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

19.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
19.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

20.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
20.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

21.meaning: I fear, I am afraid of, I stand in awe/dread — expressing the speaker's own fear, whether dread of harm or reverent awe.
21.grammar: A present-tense verb. The a- prefix marks the doer as 'I'. The final -u ending marks the ordinary (indicative) mood, used for a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual state ('I fear / I am fearing').

22.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
22.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

23.meaning: Torment, punishment, or chastisement — severe, painful suffering imposed as a penalty.
23.grammar: A singular noun. The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case, the form used for a direct object of a verb, or for the first noun of a possessive pair ('the punishment of …') when that whole phrase is itself an object.

24.meaning: a day — a day, the basic unit of daytime or a twenty-four-hour span; figuratively a time or occasion.
24.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -in ending marks the genitive case together with the indefinite 'a/an'. The genitive is the case used after prepositions or to link this noun to a preceding word ('… of a day').
24.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — a day, a span of time

25.meaning: An adjective meaning 'great', 'immense', 'mighty', or 'tremendous' — vast in size, importance, or gravity; used of things weighty and momentous.
25.grammar: An adjective on the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern (conveying a strong, established quality), carrying the genitive indefinite '-in' (tanwīn) ending. The genitive case typically appears after a preposition or when describing/qualifying a preceding genitive noun.
25.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, mighty, immense; (literally) bone, hence weightiness

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

2.meaning: "have you come to us?" — the question-marker "?" plus the past-tense verb "you came/arrived," with "us" as the destination.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb fronted by the interrogative particle a- ("is it that…?"). The -ta ending marks a single male "you" as the doer of the completed action; the suffix -nā is the object "us."

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

4.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

5.meaning: 'Our gods' — objects of worship, deities. The plural of 'ilāh' (a god/object of worship), with the attached ending meaning 'our.'
5.grammar: A plural noun, 'gods/deities,' with the possessive ending '-nā' ('our'). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case-vowel, marking the noun as possessed by ('…of us') the attached 'our.'
5.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — to worship, deify; a god, object of worship

6.meaning: "so bring us / then bring to us" — the connective "so/then" plus the command "bring!", with "us" as the one brought to.
6.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to one male; the bare stem ending in -i is the imperative form ("bring!"). The suffix -nā is the object "us," and the leading fa- means "so/then," linking it as a consequence.
6.root: ا-ت-ي (ʔ-t-y) — to come; (with object) to bring

7.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
7.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

8.meaning: "you promise us / you threaten us" — the present-tense act of pledging or warning of something to come, by a single "you," with "us" as recipient.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks a single "you" (male) as doer; the -u before the suffix is the indicative present (ongoing/general action). The suffix -nā is the object "us."

9.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
9.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

10.meaning: 'You (single male) were / used to be' — the past tense of 'to be', describing a past state, and often an ongoing or habitual condition in the past ('you used to…').
10.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) form of the verb 'to be'. The suffix -ta marks the subject as 'you', a single male. It states a condition that held in the past; paired with a following present-tense verb it often gives the sense 'you used to / you would (habitually)'.
10.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, becoming, coming to exist

11.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
11.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

12.meaning: The truthful ones — those who are sincere and speak the truth, whose words and deeds match reality. A plural describing people characterized by truthfulness and sincerity, prefixed with 'the.'
12.grammar: A masculine plural active participle ('the ones who are truthful') with the definite article 'the.' The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive (oblique) form: it marks the word either as an object of a verb or as following a preposition or possessive, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
12.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity, telling the truth

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
2.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

3.meaning: Knowledge: sure, certain knowing — grasping a thing as it truly is. As a verbal noun it names the state or body of knowledge itself.
3.grammar: A definite noun with the prefixed article 'al-' ('the'). The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being named.

4.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
4.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').
4.root: — (adverb of place)

5.meaning: The proper name of the One True God in Arabic — Allah, the unique, supreme Deity worshipped alone, without partner or equal. It is a name, not a common noun, and is not pluralized or made feminine.
5.grammar: The divine proper name. The final '-i' (kasra) is the genitive case — the case taken after a preposition or when the name is linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah'). Being a name, it carries no indefinite tanwīn.
5.root: — (the divine proper name; not derived from a triliteral root in the ordinary sense)

7.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
7.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

8.meaning: I have been sent — I was dispatched or commissioned (as a messenger) by someone with a message or task.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice of the causative form ('to be made to go, to be sent'). The attached -tu marks the subject as 'I'. Being passive, the doer is unstated, and the focus is on the one sent: 'I have been sent'.

9.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
9.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'
