10.meaning: "And yet I… / But as for me…" — a compound joining the conjunction 'and' to the contrastive particle 'but/however' (which corrects or counters a preceding statement), ending in an attached 'I'. It strongly draws attention to the speaker's own contrasting position.
10.grammar: A conjunction wa- ('and') joined to lākinna, a particle of correction that contradicts what came before. Like inna, lākinna governs the following noun or pronoun in the accusative (naṣb) and places emphasis on it; the doubled 'n' carries that emphasis. The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun, here in its accusative position as the noun of lākinna, so the whole reads an emphatic 'and yet as for me'.

11.meaning: A past-tense verb from the root of seeing, in the causative sense 'he showed / let you see / made you behold' something. So: 'he caused you (plural) to see'.
11.grammar: A perfect (past) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), in the causative (Form IV) pattern ('to make someone see' = to show). The final long vowel of the stem is a weak (defective) root letter. The attached -kum is the object 'you all'.
11.root: ر-ء-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see; (causative) to show, cause to behold

12.meaning: 'A people, a folk, a community' — a group of human beings bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared standing.
12.grammar: An indefinite collective noun. The -an ending (accusative with tanwīn, the 'n' sound) marks it as the object of an action.
12.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group, people

13.meaning: You act ignorantly; you behave foolishly without knowledge. The verb conveys being or acting in ignorance — lacking knowledge and behaving rashly because of it.
13.grammar: An imperfect (present/ongoing) verb. The ta- prefix here marks a second-person addressee, and the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'you (all)' in the indicative mood, indicating a real, ongoing action. The full -ūna (not shortened to -ū) shows the verb stands free of any particle that would cut it short.

1.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
1.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'they saw it' / 'they perceived it' (with an object 'it'). The base sense is seeing with the eyes, and by extension recognizing or witnessing something. Depending on context this form can read as a completed past act ('they saw it') or, after a conditional particle, as a prospective 'when/if they (will) see it'. The attached object pronoun makes it 'they saw/see IT'.
2.grammar: A perfect (past-form) verb. The -aw ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject: 'they' performed the act of seeing. The attached -hu is an object pronoun, 'it/him', the thing seen. While the perfect form is by default past, after a conditional particle it can carry a future/prospective force ('when/if they see it'), so the whole signals a completed — or conditionally anticipated — act of seeing by a male/mixed group upon a single object.

6.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.
6.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

7.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
7.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

10.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
10.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

11.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
11.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

12.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
12.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

14.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
14.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

15.meaning: A wind — a current of moving air, a gust or breeze. The same base noun for wind, here standing on its own as an indefinite subject. Grammatically the noun is feminine.
15.grammar: A noun with the ending -un: the -u is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence (the one doing or being something), and the final -n (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a wind'). The noun rīḥ is grammatically feminine.

16.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
16.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

17.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
17.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.

18.meaning: Painful, agonizing, deeply hurtful. An intensive adjective describing something that inflicts severe, grievous pain.
18.grammar: A masculine singular adjective on the intensive pattern faʿīl, conveying a strong, abiding quality ('truly painful'). The -un ending (tanwīn ḍamm) marks the nominative case (the case of a subject or of a noun's basic naming form), and the nunation shows it is indefinite.

2.meaning: All, every, the whole of — totality. When followed by a singular it means 'every (one)'; when followed by a definite plural or whole it means 'all of.'
2.grammar: A noun of totality, almost always joined to a following noun in the genitive ('every … / all of …'). The final -a is the accusative case, the form used when the word functions as an object of a verb.

3.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
3.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
3.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

4.meaning: By/with the command, order, or affair; conveys both a directive that must be obeyed and, more broadly, a matter or decree under someone's authority. Often denotes a divine decree or directive.
4.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'by, with, through'. The noun 'amr means a command or a matter/affair. The -i ending is genitive, which is required after a preposition and also typically links the word to a following noun ('command OF ...').
4.root: ء-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — commanding, ordering; matter, affair

5.meaning: Its Lord — 'Lord' (Rabb) denotes the Master, Owner, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, provides for, and brings a thing to its full development; here joined to a feminine possessor.
5.grammar: A noun ending in the genitive -i, the case that typically links a word to a following noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition. The attached -hā means 'its' (referring to a feminine noun). So: 'of its Lord' / 'its Lord's'.
5.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship

6.meaning: "And they came to be / and they became," from a verb that originally means "to enter upon the morning" and by extension "to end up in a certain state / to become." It describes a group transitioning into a new condition.
6.grammar: The "fa-" prefix means "so" or "and then," marking a result or sequence. The verb is in the completed (past) tense; the "-ū" ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ("they"). As one of the "sisters of kāna," this verb links a subject to a predicate state, hence "they became (something)."
6.root: ص-ب-ح (ṣ-b-ḥ) — morning / the coming of daybreak; by extension, to come to be in a state

7.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

9.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
9.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

11.meaning: 'Like that / thus / in this manner.' A comparison word meaning that something is done or is the case in the way just mentioned.
11.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like/as') prefixed to the demonstrative 'that'. Together they form a fixed adverbial expression, 'like that / thus', which does not change its ending with grammatical position.
11.root: — (a particle of comparison joined to a demonstrative; no root)

12.meaning: 'We reward / We requite' — to repay or recompense someone for their deeds, whether with good or with due consequence.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'na-' prefix means 'we'. The stem ends in a long '-ī' (a weak final root letter); in the plain indicative this final '-ī' is what is heard, giving 'we reward'.
12.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — to repay, to recompense, to requite

13.meaning: the people / the folk — a body of people, a community or group regarded collectively (here in the accusative form).
13.grammar: The l- prefix is the definite article 'the'. The final -a ending is accusative. Since the verb it follows is passive (and so takes no direct object), this accusative is adverbial — marking the circumstance or setting of the action ('before / in front of the people') rather than a thing being acted upon.
13.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to arise; a people standing together

14.meaning: Those who commit grave sins and crimes; wrongdoers who deliberately break Allah's law and cut themselves off in guilt. The word denotes hardened, culpable offenders, not those who err by accident.
14.grammar: An active participle (one who does the action) of Form IV, made definite by 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) case, so it names a group as the object of a verb or the complement of a preposition, rather than the subject.
14.root: ج-ر-م (j-r-m) — to commit a crime or grave sin

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

3.meaning: A compound particle joining the preposition 'in/about' with the relative pronoun 'what', yielding 'in that which' or 'concerning what' — pointing to the matter or subject about which something is said or done.
3.grammar: A fixed combination of the preposition 'fī' and the indeclinable relative 'mā'. Being particles, neither takes a case ending; the phrase functions as 'in/about what…'.

4.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
4.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

6.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
6.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

7.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'We made / appointed / rendered.' This very common verb can mean to create or place something, or to assign something a state or role (to make X into Y).
7.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action. The -nā ending marks 'we' as the doers. The verb often takes two objects, meaning 'to make/turn one thing into another.'
7.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, render, appoint

8.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
8.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

12.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
12.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

13.meaning: It availed / enriched / sufficed: a completed-action verb meaning something was of use or benefit, made one independent of need, or warded off a want.
13.grammar: A past-tense (completed-action) verb in Form IV, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The Form IV pattern is causative, giving the sense of 'making free of need' or 'being of avail.' The final long -ā is the verb's weak (defective) ending.
13.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — to be free of need, rich, self-sufficient

14.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
14.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.

16.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
16.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

17.meaning: Their eyes / their sights: the organs of sight, or by extension acts of seeing and glances. The plural noun denotes eyes belonging to a group.
17.grammar: A plural noun (plural of baṣar, 'sight/eye') with an attached possessive pronoun. The -u is the nominative ending, marking it typically as the subject; the suffix -hum means 'their' (masculine plural).

18.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
18.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

20.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
20.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

21.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
21.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
21.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

22.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
22.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

23.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
23.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
23.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

24.meaning: A verb meaning 'they knowingly reject / deny / repudiate.' Its distinctive sense is denying something one inwardly recognizes to be true — rejection against better knowledge.

parts.en: they (the prefix marking a third-person subject)
plural marker, with the -na of the ongoing/present

24.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, third-person masculine plural. The ya- prefix marks 'they,' and -ūna marks a plural subject and an ongoing or repeated action. The retained -na is the mark of the indicative mood, the verb's default unbroken form.
24.root: ج-ح-د (j-ḥ-d) — to deny or reject what one knows to be true

25.meaning: 'With/in the signs of…' — the preposition bi- joined to a plural noun meaning 'signs', 'tokens', or 'verses': evidences that point to a truth beyond themselves.
25.grammar: bi- is a preposition meaning 'with/in' and always takes the genitive. āyāt is a sound feminine plural; its -i ending here is genitive, the case required after the preposition, and it typically also links to a following noun ('signs OF …').
25.root: ء-ي-ي / ء-و-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token

26.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
26.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

27.meaning: And it closed in / encompassed — to surround completely and descend upon, especially of a punishment or consequence that envelops people and leaves no escape.
27.grammar: A past-tense verb (a hollow root, whose middle letter appears as the long 'ā'). It is third-person masculine singular ('he/it did') and complete in the past; it characteristically governs a following 'with/upon' to name those whom the encirclement befalls. The prefixed wa- simply means 'and.'

28.meaning: An expression meaning 'at them' or 'with them' — the preposition 'bi' (with, by, at) joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group). The exact shade ('at/by/with them') depends on the verb it accompanies.
28.grammar: A preposition (bi-, 'with/by/at') with the attached pronoun -him ('them,' for a group of males). The pronoun is in the genitive, the case always required after a preposition.

29.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
29.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

30.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
30.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
30.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

31.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
31.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

32.meaning: 'They mock / ridicule / hold in derision.' The ongoing or habitual act of making a mockery of someone, scoffing and jeering at them.
32.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb of Form X (the ista-/-stah- pattern). The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural acting in the present or habitual ('they keep mocking'); the -ūna ending also signals the indicative (uninterrupted) mood. The Form X shape here intensifies the sense of deliberately making a mockery.
32.root: ه-ز-أ (h-z-ʾ) — to mock, ridicule, scoff, deride

1.meaning: "And indeed / and most certainly" — combines 'and' with the emphatic 'la-' and the particle 'qad'; before a past-tense verb 'qad' affirms that the action has definitely and already happened, reinforced into 'and indeed it surely did'.
1.grammar: The conjunction 'and' plus the emphatic 'la-' ('surely') plus the particle 'qad'. With a past-tense verb, 'qad' stresses that the act is real and completed ('has indeed happened'); together they form a strong oath-like affirmation. These are function words and are not inflected.

2.meaning: 'We destroyed / We caused to perish' — to bring about ruin, annihilation, or downfall. Combines the verb 'to destroy / cause to perish' with the subject 'we'.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb. The attached '-nā' ending is the subject 'we' — it marks the doers of the action as a group including the speaker, with the action completed and in the past.
2.root: ه-ل-ك (h-l-k) — to perish, be destroyed; (causative) to destroy

3.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
3.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

4.meaning: Around you / in your surroundings — the area encircling or in the vicinity of the addressees. The base word means 'around/about', joined to 'you (plural)'.
4.grammar: An adverb of place, 'around/surrounding', fixed in the accusative form (the -a after ḥawl). The attached -kum addresses a group ('you all'), yielding 'around you'.
4.root: ح-و-ل (ḥ-w-l) — to surround, encircle; turning about

5.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
5.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

6.meaning: 'the towns / settlements'. The plural of qarya, a town, village, or settled habitation — any gathered dwelling-place of people.
6.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of qarya. It ends in a 'restricted' final long vowel written as alif maqṣūra (ى), which stays the same in all cases — its case is understood from context rather than shown by a changing vowel. The prefixed al- makes it definite ('the towns').
6.root: ق-ر-ي (q-r-y) — to gather; a gathering-place, town/settlement

8.meaning: 'The signs / the verses' — the plural of 'sign,' referring to clear indicators, proofs, miracles, or the verses of revelation that point to truth.
8.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun ('the signs'), made definite by the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The sound feminine plural takes the -i ending when it is an object of a verb or linked after a preposition or possessor — that is, when it is grammatically governed rather than serving as the subject.

9.meaning: 'So that they may / perhaps they will.' A particle expressing hope, expectation, or purpose, fused with the pronoun 'them'; it introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome.

parts.en: perhaps / so that / in hope that

9.grammar: The particle laʿalla ('perhaps, in the hope that, so that') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), which serves as its subject. Laʿalla belongs to a family of particles that put a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; -hum is that fixed object form. It conveys hope or an intended purpose rather than certainty.

10.meaning: To return, go back, or turn back — to come back to a place, state, or point of origin. Used of a group: 'they return / come back'.
10.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they return'). The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks an ongoing or repeated action by a group of males or a mixed group. The -ūna 'indicative' ending appears when nothing precedes the verb to shorten it.

1.meaning: "So if not / then were it not for" — combines 'so/then' with 'lawlā', which introduces a 'were it not for…' condition (something whose absence would change the outcome) and can also urge 'why not…?'.

parts.en: were it not for / why not

1.grammar: A connective 'fa' ('so, then', often marking a result) plus the particle 'lawlā'. As a conditional particle 'lawlā' sets up 'were it not for X (then Y would not be)'; as an incitement it means 'why do you not…?'. It is a function word, not inflected.

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: Past-tense verb (reflexive form), third person plural: 'they took for themselves, adopted, chose.' A completed act of taking something on as one's own.
4.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb in a reflexive pattern (taking something for oneself). The '-ū' ending (with silent trailing alif) marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural). The opening 'i-' is a helping vowel that lets the cluster of consonants be pronounced.
4.root: أ-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, grasp

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
6.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
6.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: 'An offering / a sacrifice; that which is offered to draw near'. The noun qurbān denotes something presented to Allah as a means of seeking closeness to Him.
8.grammar: An indefinite noun. The final -an is nunation in the accusative case — the form a noun takes as a direct object (the thing offered or presented).
8.root: ق-ر-ب (q-r-b) — nearness; that which brings one near

9.meaning: A noun meaning 'gods / deities' — the plural of ilāh, objects taken as worthy of worship besides Allah. It denotes claimed divine beings in general.
9.grammar: A plural noun, indefinite ('gods'), in the accusative case marked by tanwīn. The word ends in a tā' marbūṭah, which is normally silent in pause but is pronounced as -t- when a case-vowel and tanwīn follow it; combined with the accusative tanwīn this is sounded as -tan, so the full ending is ālihatan (not a bare -an). The accusative typically marks a noun as the object of a verb or the focus of certain particles.
9.root: ا-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, that which is worshipped

10.meaning: A particle of retraction meaning 'rather,' 'no, but,' or 'nay' — it cancels or sets aside what was just said and shifts to a corrected or contrasting statement that follows.
10.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it never changes form). Its function is to redirect the discourse: it dismisses a prior idea and introduces what is actually the case.

11.meaning: 'they went astray / erred' — to lose the right way, to wander off into error or misguidance.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb with the -ū ending meaning 'they' (masculine plural). It conveys a completed action: 'they went astray / erred.'
11.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, lose the way, go astray

12.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
12.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.

13.meaning: 'And that' — a connective 'and' plus the demonstrative 'that', pointing to something distant or already mentioned (masculine).
13.grammar: Connective 'and' + a masculine singular demonstrative pronoun, 'that (one)'. Demonstratives in Arabic do not change for grammatical case; the -ka element is a particle directing attention to a distant referent.

15.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
15.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

16.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
16.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
16.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

17.meaning: They fabricate or invent falsely — to forge a lie, concoct something untrue and attribute it where it does not belong. The verb specifically names inventing falsehood and slander out of nothing.
17.grammar: Present-tense verb in the (form VIII) pattern, third-person masculine plural. The ya- prefix marks the third person and, together with the -ūna ending, yields 'they' (masculine plural) acting in ongoing/present time. The retained -na is the mark of the indicative ('they are fabricating / they fabricate').

1.meaning: 'And when / and at the time when' — the connective 'and' joined to a word that points to a past moment or circumstance ('when'), introducing the recollection of an event or situation.
1.grammar: A connective particle plus a time-word. The wa- prefix means 'and'. 'Idh' is an invariable adverb pointing to a definite time in the past ('when, at the moment that'); it has no case ending and typically introduces a clause recalling a past event.

3.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
3.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

4.meaning: A band of people, a group of supporters, kinsmen, or followers — those who rally to a person; also a small body of men.
4.grammar: A noun. The -an ending is accusative with nunation (the doubled 'n' sound). After a comparative adjective, an accusative noun like this commonly specifies the respect in which the comparison holds — answering 'in what?' ('… in men/followers').
4.root: ن-ف-ر (n-f-r) — to go forth, rally; a troop/band

5.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
5.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

6.meaning: A noun meaning 'the jinn' — a class of unseen beings created from smokeless fire, possessing free will and accountability like humankind.
6.grammar: A definite noun with the article al- ('the'). The -i (genitive) ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in a possessive 'of' relationship.
6.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal, be hidden from sight

7.meaning: They listen, give ear, or pay attention; this verb pattern conveys actively and deliberately listening to something, lending one's ear rather than merely hearing in passing.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb in a reflexive/middle-voice (form VIII) pattern, which here adds the sense of taking in a sound for oneself — listening attentively rather than merely hearing. The prefix ya- marks a third-person ('he/they') subject, and the ending -ūna marks a male plural subject in an ongoing or habitual action: 'they listen / are listening.'

8.meaning: The Qur'an — the recited Scripture; literally 'the Recitation' or 'the Reading'.
8.grammar: A definite noun (carrying 'al-', 'the') on the verbal-noun pattern fuʿlān, denoting the act/thing of reciting. The final '-a' marks the accusative case, which most often signals that the word is the direct object of a verb.
8.root: ق-ر-ء (q-r-ʾ) — reciting, reading aloud, gathering words together

9.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
9.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

11.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

13.meaning: A connector meaning 'then, when' — it joins to what came before ('then/so') and sets up a 'when…' clause whose outcome follows. It frames a moment: 'and then, at the point when…'.
13.grammar: A compound of the connecting particle fa- ('then/so', linking to the preceding statement) and lammā, a particle meaning 'when' that introduces a past circumstance and leads the listener to expect a following result clause.

14.meaning: It was decided, decreed, or settled — a matter brought to a final verdict and concluded; to be judged and disposed of with finality.
14.grammar: A past-tense passive verb, 'it was decreed/judged' — the vowel pattern qu-i marks it as passive (done to an unnamed subject rather than by a stated doer). Its root ends in a weak letter, which here appears as final -ya; the form is third-person masculine singular ('it was settled / the matter was concluded').

15.meaning: They turned away, turned their backs, or went off in retreat; to wheel around and depart, often signalling rejection or withdrawal from something faced.
15.grammar: A past-tense verb in an intensive (form II) pattern, which adds force to the bare sense of 'turning.' The plural -ū ending (here written -aw because the verb's last root letter is weak) marks the doers as 'they' — a group of males who completed the action.
15.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to turn, be near, take charge / turn away

16.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
16.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

17.meaning: Their people — the folk, nation, or community to which they belong; one's own kin and tribe. 'Qawm' denotes a body of people bound together as a group.
17.grammar: A singular collective noun with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' ending is genitive — the form a noun takes after a preposition, or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of their people').
17.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — standing, rising; a people who stand together

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

3.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
3.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

4.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'we heard / we listened' — the act of perceiving sound or a message, often carrying the further nuance of heeding or taking in what was said.
4.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb. The attached ending -nā marks the subject as 'we', so the action is something a group did and finished: 'we heard'.
4.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — hearing, listening

5.meaning: 'A writing / a prescribed decree' — that which is written down; by extension a fixed ordinance, an appointed term, or a binding decree.
5.grammar: An indefinite noun in the accusative case: the -an ending (the 'an' sound with nunation) marks the object of a verb or a related role, and signals an indefinite 'a writing/decree'. The pattern 'kitāb' is the verbal noun denoting a written thing.

6.meaning: 'It was sent down / revealed': the act of being caused to descend, used especially of revelation brought down from Allah. The passive form puts the focus on the thing sent down rather than on the sender.
6.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in Form IV (anzala 'to send down' → unzila 'was sent down'). The prefix is only the u- vowel carried on the connecting hamza; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ز-ل), not part of the prefix. The internal vowel pattern u–i marks it as passive ('was/were sent down'), with no named doer. The final -a marks the subject as 'he/it', a single masculine thing, and signals completed action.
6.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (Form IV) to send down

7.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
7.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

8.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
8.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
8.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

9.meaning: Mūsā (Moses) — the proper name of the prophet. As a name it has no Arabic root meaning; it is a non-inflecting (indeclinable) noun whose ending does not change for case.
9.grammar: A proper name ending in a fixed long -ā (written as alif maqṣūra). It is fully indeclinable (invariable): the final -ā never changes, so the word shows no case distinction at all — it looks and sounds identical whether subject, object, or possessor. (This is unlike a diptote, which still alternates between two case vowels; here there is no alternation.)

10.meaning: Confirming, verifying, attesting to the truth of something — declaring that a thing is true and corroborating it.
10.grammar: An active participle of the intensive (fa''ala) pattern, naming the doer of the action ('one confirming'). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, often marking a noun as an object or describing the manner/state in which something occurs ('as a confirmer').

11.meaning: To / for that which — a preposition 'to, for' joined to a relative word meaning 'what' or 'that which'.
11.grammar: A combination of the preposition li- ('to, for') with the relative pronoun mā ('that which'). Together they introduce something toward or for which an action is directed; mā itself does not change for case.

12.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
12.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
12.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

13.meaning: 'His two hands' — literally a dual 'two hands' with 'his' attached. Often used idiomatically for what lies 'in front of' or 'before' someone (i.e. between his hands).
13.grammar: The noun 'yad' (hand) in its dual form 'two hands'. The -ay ending is the dual in the genitive/accusative state (as opposed to -ā for the subject case), used after prepositions or in possessive links. The attached 'hi' means 'his' (the -i vowel of 'hi' harmonizing after the -ay). In construct, the dual's final -n drops before the pronoun.

14.meaning: 'He guides / leads on the right way' — to show someone the correct path, direct them rightly, or lead them to a goal, whether literally or in matters of belief and conduct.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: the ya- prefix means 'he'. The verb ends in a long -ī (a weak final letter); in this indicative form the long vowel stands in place of the usual -u mood marker, still conveying a plain, ongoing statement ('he guides').
14.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the way, leading rightly

15.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
15.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

16.meaning: 'The truth', 'the right', 'what is rightfully due' — that which is real, correct, and justly owed; the opposite of falsehood and wrongdoing.
16.grammar: A definite masculine noun (the al- prefix means 'the'). The -i ending is genitive, the case typically taken after a preposition or when the word links to a preceding noun ('… of the truth / by right').
16.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, rightness, that which is established and due

17.meaning: "and to / toward" — the connective "and" joined to the preposition meaning "to, toward, up to (an end-point)."
17.grammar: A particle cluster: the connective wa- ("and") plus the preposition ilā ("to/toward"), which indicates direction or destination and puts the following noun into the genitive case. Particles do not inflect.

19.meaning: 'Straight / upright / undeviating' — describing something that runs true without bending or wandering; applied to a 'path' it means a direct, correct way that leads soundly to its goal.
19.grammar: An active participle (a describing word, 'straight/upright') from a verb meaning 'to be/become straight'. It is indefinite, and the -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn'. As a describing word it normally follows and agrees with the noun it modifies, matching that noun in being indefinite and in the genitive case.

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: 'And believe! / have faith, trust' — a command to believe in, place faith and secure trust in something. Prefixed 'wa' adds 'and.'
5.grammar: 'And' (wa) plus a command (imperative) verb to a masculine plural 'you.' The verb comes from a causative (Form IV) pattern meaning 'to have faith / give one's trust'; the '-ū' ending directs the order to a group ('you all believe!').
5.root: ا-م-ن / ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — faith, security, trust, safety

6.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
6.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

8.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
8.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

9.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
9.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

10.meaning: Sins, wrongdoings, faults; offenses attributed to a 'your (plural)' possessor.
10.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun, 'sins', with the attached pronoun '-kum' = 'your' (for a group). The '-i' ending is genitive: it appears because the noun is possessed ('the sins OF you') and also occurs after a preposition.

12.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
12.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

13.meaning: A punishment / torment — painful chastisement or suffering imposed as a penalty. The word names the punishment itself, stated indefinitely ('a punishment').
13.grammar: A noun, 'punishment/torment'. The final -in (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and genitive in case — the form used after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of a punishment').

14.meaning: Painful / agonizing: causing intense pain; said of something that grieves and torments deeply. An intensive adjective, so 'sorely painful'. Indefinite ('a painful …').
14.grammar: An indefinite adjective on an intensive pattern (conveying 'deeply/sorely painful'). The ending -in shows both indefiniteness (the final -n, nunation: 'a painful one') and the genitive case (the -i vowel), the case that an adjective takes to match a genitive noun it describes or that follows a preposition.

1.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
1.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

2.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
2.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: Then he/it is not; a negation that denies a present state or quality — 'is not the case', 'is not so'. The base word laysa specifically negates being or existence in the present.
6.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'so' or 'then'. The stem laysa is a special negating verb meaning 'is not', used to deny a present state. The -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it is not').
6.root: ل-ي-س (l-y-s) — negation of being; 'is not' (defective verb)

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
8.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

9.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
9.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

10.meaning: A special negating verb meaning 'is not / are not.' It denies that something is currently the case, functioning to negate a statement in the present, and it inflects for person like a verb.
10.grammar: A hollow negating verb fixed in form for the third-person masculine singular ('he/it is not'); the -a ending belongs to its frozen past-tense shape. Though past in form, it negates in the present. It introduces a subject and a predicate, denying the link between them. The prefix wa means 'and'.

11.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
11.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

12.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
12.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

13.meaning: Other than Him / apart from Him / besides Him. A relational word expressing the idea of being below, short of, or to the exclusion of something or someone.

parts.en: other than, apart from, besides, below

13.grammar: A relational noun/quasi-preposition meaning 'apart from / instead of'. It is followed by a possessive pronoun -hi ('Him'), which puts it in the genitive 'of' relationship; the kasra written under the pronoun reflects this genitive linkage.

14.meaning: Protectors, close allies, guardians, intimate friends — those bound to one another in loyalty, support, and mutual responsibility. A 'walī' is one who is near and takes charge of another's affairs; the plural gathers many such allies.
14.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of walī. The final -u is the nominative ending, the state a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified (as in 'they are allies').

15.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'those' — pointing to people or things that are distant or already known. It singles out a group ('those ones', 'it is those who').
15.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. It is fixed in form (no case endings). The -ka element signals distance/remoteness, pointing to something far off or notable. It can refer to people of either gender.

16.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
16.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

17.meaning: Means 'straying / error / being lost' — wandering off the right path, the opposite of guidance, whether literally losing one's way or going astray in belief and conduct.
17.grammar: An abstract noun: 'straying / error.' The -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite) — the case a noun takes after a preposition or in a possessive link, e.g. 'in an error.' The long -ā- belongs to this noun-pattern.
17.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way

18.meaning: Means 'clear / plain / making manifest' — something that is evident in itself and also makes other things plain, leaving no ambiguity.
18.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) from a pattern that often carries the sense 'making clear' as well as 'being clear.' The -in ending is the genitive with 'tanwīn' (the -n marking it indefinite), the form taken after a preposition or when describing a genitive noun — i.e. it agrees with a preceding indefinite noun in the genitive ('a clear …').
18.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, distinct; to make evident

1.meaning: A compound opening a question and a negation at once: roughly 'and have … not …?' or 'is it not the case that …?'. It combines a questioning particle, the connector 'and', and a negative that places the following verb in the past, often expecting the listener to agree.
1.grammar: Three particles fused together: the interrogative 'a-' (turning the statement into a question), the connector 'wa' ('and'), and the negator 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and shifts its meaning into the past ('has not / did not'), and it puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (vowel-less) form. The combination often invites the listener to affirm ('have you not …?').

2.meaning: To see, perceive, or behold — and, by extension, to realize, observe, or come to recognize. The bare form here is the 'cut-short' (jussive) shape used after certain particles, so it reads 'they (do not) see'.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb in its shortened (jussive) form, used after particles such as those that negate the past or express purpose/condition. The third-person masculine plural subject 'they' here takes the distinct jussive plural ending '-aw' (written wāw + a silent 'alif al-fāriqa). This '-aw' is the jussive paradigm's own ending in its own right, not the indicative '-ūna' with the 'na' stripped off.

3.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
3.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
4.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
4.root: — (proper name)

5.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
5.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

6.meaning: 'He created' — to bring into being, to originate and shape something that did not exist before, from the root denoting creation and the fashioning of things from nothing.
6.grammar: Past tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'), completed action ('he created'). This is a form I verb of the CaCaCa pattern. The masculine singular 'he' here is the unmarked (zero-suffix) form — there is no separate person ending; the final -a is the inherent stem vowel of the base pattern, not a person or tense suffix.
6.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — creating, originating, shaping

7.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
7.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

8.meaning: 'and the earth' — the ground, land, or the planet earth; the world we stand upon, often paired with the heavens to mean all of creation.
8.grammar: A feminine noun, prefixed with 'and' and 'the.' The -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or a noun governed by certain particles.

9.meaning: 'And not' — the conjunction wa- ('and') joined to lam, a particle that negates a verb and pushes its meaning into the completed past ('did not …').
9.grammar: A connector wa- ('and') plus the negative particle lam. Lam negates a following present-tense verb but turns its sense into the past: 'has not / did not …'. It also causes that verb to take the jussive (clipped) ending.

12.meaning: Means '(being) able / capable / having power to do', preceded by an attached 'with/by'. The core word is an active participle: 'one who is able', 'a possessor of power'.
12.grammar: The prefix bi- is a preposition ('with/by'), often added for emphasis after a negation. qādir is an active participle ('one who is able'). The ending -in is indefinite genitive (tanwīn / 'nunation'): the genitive case is required because the word follows the preposition bi-, and the final -n marks it as indefinite ('an able one').
12.root: ق-د-ر (q-d-r) — power, capability, measuring out, decree

14.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
14.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

16.meaning: 'The dead' — those who have died or are without life; the lifeless, as a group.
16.grammar: A definite plural noun/adjective ('the dead'). It is of a plural pattern that ends in a fixed long -ā, so its ending does not change with grammatical position; it refers collectively to those who are dead.

17.meaning: An emphatic 'Yes indeed!' — a particle of affirmation used specifically to overturn a preceding negative or negative question, asserting 'Nay, rather it IS so'. It affirms the positive against a denial.

parts.en: yes indeed / nay, rather (it is so)

17.grammar: An indeclinable affirmative particle (it does not change form or take case endings). Its special function is to answer a negative statement or question with a strong positive, contradicting the negation.

19.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
19.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

21.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
21.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
21.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

22.meaning: All-powerful, fully able, ever-capable — possessing complete and effective power to do whatever is willed; one whose ability never falls short.
22.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses a deep, abiding quality ('thoroughly able'). The final -un is the indefinite nominative (nunation) — the doubled-n shows no 'the', and the -u base vowel marks the nominative case, used when the word is a subject or a predicate ('… is all-powerful').

1.meaning: "and (on the) day" — the conjunction "and" joined to the noun for "day," a single daytime period or, more broadly, an appointed day or time of judgment/event.
1.grammar: The wa- prefix is the conjunction "and." The -a ending on the noun is accusative; on a word for "day" this frequently marks it as an adverb of time ("on the day …"), or marks it as the object of a verb.

3.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
3.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

4.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
4.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

5.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
5.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
5.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

6.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
6.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').
6.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — fire, blaze, burning

7.meaning: "Is it not …? / Is … not …?" A questioning "is not," combining the question-marker "a-" with the negative verb "laysa" ("is not"), used to ask a question that expects the answer "yes, it is."
7.grammar: The negating verb laysa ("is/are not") prefixed with the question-marker a- ("…?"). Such "is it not …?" questions typically invite agreement ("yes, indeed it is"). Laysa is a special verb that negates a statement of being; it carries no tense-ending of the ordinary kind here.

8.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
8.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

9.meaning: 'With the truth / by means of what is true and right.' Combines the preposition 'with/by' and 'the truth' — that which is real, established, correct, and rightfully due, as opposed to falsehood.
9.grammar: A noun governed by the attached preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -i ending is the genitive case, which is required after a preposition; here it links 'the truth' to 'with', giving 'with the truth'.
9.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, reality, that which is established and due

10.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

11.meaning: Yes indeed / nay, rather — an affirmative reply used specifically to contradict a preceding negative and assert the positive: 'Yes (it is so), on the contrary.'
11.grammar: A response particle. Unlike a plain 'yes', it is used to overturn a negative statement or question and affirm what was denied. It does not inflect; the final long '-ā' is part of its fixed form.

12.meaning: "By our Lord!" An oath upon "the Lord" — the Master, Sustainer, and Nurturer who owns, cares for, and brings to completion — with "our" attached. The opening "wa" here functions as the oath-word "by."
12.grammar: The noun rabb ("Lord") with the attached possessive "-nā" ("our"). The -i ending is the genitive case, which here follows the oath-particle wa- ("by"); the genitive is the form a noun takes after a preposition or oath-word, or when linked to a preceding noun ("… of …").
12.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship

13.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
13.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

14.meaning: So taste! — a command to a group to 'taste' or experience something, often used figuratively of undergoing a consequence or punishment.
14.grammar: A command (imperative). The fa- prefix means 'so' or 'then', linking it to what precedes. The -ū ending directs the order to a masculine plural addressee ('you all'): 'so taste!'. The final silent alif is a spelling convention after this plural ending.

15.meaning: The punishment, chastisement, or torment — a penalty inflicted as retribution, especially the painful suffering of divine reckoning.
15.grammar: A definite masculine noun ('the punishment'). The final -a is the accusative ending, which generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb or the subject/predicate after certain particles.
15.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, torment; the inflicting of pain

16.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
16.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

17.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
17.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
17.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

18.meaning: A verb meaning 'you disbelieve', 'you reject faith', or 'you are ungrateful' — to refuse to believe, to deny the truth, or to be ungrateful, addressed to a group.
18.grammar: Present/imperfect verb, second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix marks the second person ('you') and the -ūna ending marks a masculine-plural subject in the indicative mood (ongoing or habitual action). The root joins the ideas of denying faith and being ungrateful — covering over a truth or a blessing.
18.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to disbelieve, deny, be ungrateful, cover over

1.meaning: A command meaning 'so be patient' or 'so endure steadfastly.' It calls for patient perseverance: bearing hardship, restraining oneself, and holding firm without complaint. The opening 'fa-' connects it to what precedes, giving the sense 'and so…' or 'therefore…'
1.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single male: 'be patient!' The vowelless final consonant (sukun on the -r) is the standard ending of a direct order. The prefixed 'fa-' is a connective particle meaning 'so' or 'therefore,' linking the command to a preceding statement.

2.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
2.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

4.meaning: 'Possessors of / owners of / people of' — a plural construct word meaning those endowed with or characterized by whatever follows it (e.g. 'those of understanding'). It has no singular of its own form and is always joined to a following noun.
4.grammar: A masculine plural noun used only in the construct state (always followed by another noun, 'possessors OF ...'). The -ū ending is the nominative plural form, marking it as the subject or doer of a sentence. The trailing alif is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
4.root: — (a word for 'possessors of', having no verbal root)

5.meaning: Of firm resolve; of determination and steadfastness. Al-'azm refers to a settled, unshakeable decision or inner strength of will — the quality that keeps one committed to a course despite difficulty.

parts.en: genitive (kasra) ending, arising because the word follows a preposition or stands as the second term of an idafa construct

5.grammar: The noun 'azm carries the definite article al-. The -i ending (kasra) is the genitive case, arising because the word follows a preposition or stands as the second term of an idafa construct. The phrase typically appears as 'those of firm resolve' (ulu l-'azmi), where the genitive marks possession of this quality.

6.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
6.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

7.meaning: 'the messengers' — the envoys sent by Allah, taken definitely as a known group.
7.grammar: The prefix al- ('the') makes it definite (its 'l' assimilates to the following 'r'). The base is the broken plural of rasūl. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the messengers') or follows a preposition.

8.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
8.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

9.meaning: You seek to hasten; you try to rush or accelerate something before its appointed time. The form implies an eager, impatient striving to bring something about more quickly.

parts.en: seek to hasten / seek to rush (Form X stem)

9.grammar: Form X verb (istaf'ala pattern), present-tense jussive, second-person masculine singular. The ta- prefix marks 'you'. The sukun (absence of a vowel) on the final letter is the jussive marker — this form appears after negation (lā) or in conditional/prohibitive constructions, indicating a command, prohibition, or conditional clause rather than a simple ongoing statement.

10.meaning: 'For them / to them / theirs' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the pronoun 'them,' expressing that something pertains, belongs, or is owed to that group.
10.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to'), whose vowel becomes -a before an attached pronoun, joined to -hum ('them'). It commonly expresses possession or benefit — 'theirs / for them.' Particles like this carry no case or tense of their own.

11.meaning: As though they / as if they (were) — the comparison particle 'ka-anna' ('as if', likening one thing to another) joined to the pronoun 'they', introducing a supposed or apparent state.
11.grammar: A compound particle: 'ka-' ('like/as') fused with the emphatic 'anna' ('that') to form 'ka-anna' = 'as if'.
