It governs the following pronoun '-hum' ('they'), which takes the accusative form as its subject. It sets up a comparison: things appear as though a certain (often untrue) state held.

12.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
12.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
12.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

13.meaning: They see; they behold or perceive with their eyes. Can extend to mental perception — 'they consider' or 'they come to see' — depending on context.

parts.en: see / behold (verb stem from root ر-أ-ي)

13.grammar: Form I imperfect (present/future), third-person masculine plural. The ya- prefix signals third-person and the -na suffix confirms a masculine plural subject — together meaning 'they (men/those people) see'. The combination ya-…-na is the standard mark of third-person masculine plural in the present tense.

14.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
14.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

15.meaning: 'They are promised / threatened' — something pledged to a group, whether a promised good or a warned-of consequence, with the group as recipient.
15.grammar: A present-tense passive verb (the subjects receive the action). The yu- prefix with the inner vowel pattern signals 'are being …' (done to them). The -ūna ending marks 'they' (plural) in ongoing/repeated time.
15.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — to promise, pledge, warn of what is to come

16.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

16.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.

17.meaning: To stay, to remain, to linger or tarry in a place for a span of time.
17.grammar: Present-tense verb with a third-person masculine plural subject: the ya- prefix plus the -ū ending together mean 'they (men/people).' The plain indicative would end in -ūna; here the shortened -ū (with a silent written alif) shows the verb is in a dependent mood — the form used after certain particles or in negation, e.g. 'they did not remain / that they remain.'

18.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
18.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

19.meaning: An hour; more broadly a span of time, a moment, or the appointed 'Hour' (the climactic moment of resurrection and judgement). Its underlying sense is a defined stretch or point of time.
19.grammar: A feminine noun in the indefinite accusative. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('an hour, some hour') and as accusative — the case used for the direct object of a verb or for adverbial expressions of time and extent (e.g. 'for an hour').
19.root: س-و-ع (s-w-ʿ) — a moment or span of time

20.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
20.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

21.meaning: A day; the period of daylight from dawn to sunset, or more broadly a twenty-four-hour day. Used to denote a span of time and often implies a moment of reckoning or measure.

parts.en: indefinite genitive tanwin (double kasra / nunation), marking the word as indefinite and in the genitive case

21.grammar: The word nahār is an indefinite masculine noun. The -in ending (tanwin al-jarr) marks it as indefinite and in the genitive case, arising after a preposition or within constructions that require the genitive. The shadda that may appear on the initial nūn in connected Quranic recitation is a phonological assimilation effect from a preceding word and is not part of the intrinsic form of nahār itself.
21.root: ن-ه-ر (n-h-r) — daylight, flowing brightness (the root also underlies 'river', carrying connotations of abundant light or flow)

22.meaning: A conveying / a notification / a sufficient message — the act and content of delivering communication so it reaches and informs its hearers; that which is enough to make the point.
22.grammar: A verbal noun meaning 'a conveying / proclamation that reaches its hearers'. The -un ending is indefinite nominative (tanwīn al-ḍamm): it marks the word as 'a ___' (unspecified) and as the subject or predicate of a sentence (the thing spoken about).
22.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — to reach, arrive at, attain; to convey

23.meaning: 'So/then — is it the case that…?' A linking 'then' joined to an interrogative particle that introduces a yes/no question, often carrying a sense of urging, challenge, or expectation ('will you not…?').
23.grammar: A compound of the connective fa- ('so, then', linking to what precedes) and the question particle hal, which turns a statement into a yes/no question and frequently implies expectation or exhortation. Particles like this are invariable — they take no case or mood ending.

24.meaning: 'It/he is destroyed / brought to ruin' — to be annihilated or made to perish. This is the passive sense: the subject undergoes destruction at another's hand rather than causing it.

parts.en: he/it (third-person masculine present prefix, passive vowel)

24.grammar: A present-tense verb in the passive voice: the 'yu-' prefix with the internal 'a' vowel pattern means 'he/it is (being) destroyed' — the action is done TO the subject. The '-u' ending is the ordinary present-tense form for an ongoing action.

25.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
25.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

26.meaning: 'The people / the folk' — a community or body of people, often a tribe or nation considered collectively. Grammatically singular but referring to a group.
26.grammar: A definite noun ('the people') marked by the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The '-u' ending is the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence (the one doing or being something).
26.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — standing, rising; a people who stand together

27.meaning: The defiantly disobedient; those who have stepped outside the bounds set by Allah through willful, persistent transgression. Fisq connotes not mere sin but a deliberate breaking away from proper limits.

parts.en: defiantly disobedient one (active participle stem from root ف-س-ق)

27.grammar: Al-fāsiqūna is a sound masculine plural of the Form I active participle fāsiq, with the definite article. The -ūna ending is the nominative plural marker for the 'sound masculine plural' pattern, indicating that the word functions as the subject or predicate of a sentence. When it occurs in accusative/genitive contexts the ending shifts to -īna.
27.root: ف-س-ق (f-s-q) — transgression, stepping outside proper limits, moral deviation
